A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VTBC initiatives can be successful in reducing car use, but that the scale and sustainability of this effect will depend on a range of factors, not least the nature of the initiative, the context within which it is implemented and the evaluation design.

The main takeaway from our work is that
evaluation is not just a matter of measuring the effectiveness of a particular measure, it is about understanding how and why a measure works, so that it can be applied to other situations.

the evaluation of voluntary travel behaviour initiatives is a critical element of their success, and that a consistent approach to the evaluation of VTB initiatives can help to build a stronger evidence-base for the role of soft measures.
evaluation of VTBC measures is not a luxury, it is an essential part of the process, and that a consistent approach to evaluation is needed, to ensure that lessons can be learned and shared.
